text: Winning proposals are shorter. In Proposify's data on 742,137 proposals sent in 2025, the average winner ran 11 pages and the average loser ran 13. Two extra pages rarely add proof. They usually add hesitation.

A proposal gets about two and a half days. Proposify's 2026 report: from the moment a buyer opens a proposal to the deal closing, the average is 2.5 days. The decision is fast. Your follow-up should be too.

Buyers spent 25.3 minutes on proposals they signed and 15.8 on the ones they turned down (Proposify, 2026). Time is the signal. A Recto link shows how long they stayed on each page and how far they got, so you know which follow-up to write.

29% of freelance invoices are paid at least a day late. That's Bonsai's analysis of three years of invoicing data. The same study found over 75% of those late invoices were paid within 14 days of the due date. One polite reminder on day one does a lot of work.

Open Page: ANA and the 4A's put the average cost of a pitch for a non-incumbent agency at $204,461 (The Cost of the Pitch, 2023). Agencies and studios, do you track what a pitch costs you? Hours, people, spec work. What's your number?

When a client prints your proposal, you're 84% less likely to win the job. That's from Better Proposals' 2020 report on $1.48 billion of closed deals. A printout usually means a meeting you're not in. Design page one for that table.

Seven. Better Proposals found its best-converting proposals had an average of 7 sections. Proposify's 2026 data landed on the same number for winning proposals. Problem, approach, scope, timeline, proof, price, next step. That's seven.

Send it within 24 hours. In Better Proposals' 2020 data, proposals sent within a day of talking to the client were 19.1% more likely to win and were signed in about 6 days. Wait three or four days to send, and signing took almost 12.

Sign it before you send it. Proposify found that when the sender signed first, close rates rose 65% and deals closed 25% faster (2026). Your signature says the offer is real. Recto documents end with a signature block, so yours can be on the page before theirs.
Freelancers spend about 20 days a year chasing late payments, according to UK research by IPSE. Twenty working days. A month of the year spent asking for money you've already earned.

Sorani Kurdish writes most of its vowels as letters: ە ێ ۆ و ی. Arabic usually leaves short vowels out. So Kurdish text has a different rhythm and more of those letters per line, and a font drawn only for Arabic can look fine until the first Kurdish paragraph. Test with real Kurdish copy.

Proposals travel. Proposify found close rates rose 20% when more than one stakeholder viewed the proposal (2026). Someone forwards it to the person with the budget. Send a link, not an attachment, so the second reader gets the same document as the first.

Where reading time goes: 38.2% on the introduction, 27% on pricing, 34.8% on everything else combined. Better Proposals measured it in 2020. The intro and the price do two-thirds of the work. Write those two first, and best.

Price was the top reason clients chose an agency, by a wide margin. In ANA and 4A's research (2023), 62% of clients named cost/price. Creative execution came second at 45%, the big idea third at 36%. Great work gets you shortlisted. A clear price gets you picked.

Proposify found proposals with interactive pricing won twice as many deals (2026). Clients want to try options: fewer rounds, an extra deliverable, a longer retainer. Recto pricing tables multiply and total themselves, so 'what if we drop the video?' gets a new total in the meeting, not tomorrow.

71% of freelancers have had trouble getting paid at some point in their career. Freelancers Union surveyed 5,358 freelancers for that number. If it has happened to you, it isn't because you're bad at business. It's the most common story in this work.

Open Page: Better Proposals found that proposals with a cover were 3.6% more likely to win. Small, but measurable. Do you design a cover for every proposal, or go straight to the point? Show us how you open.

Clients keep their agency two times out of three. That's what clients told ANA and the 4A's about their most recent agency review (2023). Pitching against an incumbent isn't pitching against their work. It's pitching against the relationship.

83% of winning proposals in Proposify's 2026 data included images, about 12 on average. Not decoration. Proof. A before and after, the team at work, a page from a past project. If a sentence can be a picture, the picture is usually the stronger page.
34 minutes. That's how long a proposal sat, on average, before the buyer opened it (Proposify, 2026). They're waiting for it. Send it while the conversation is still warm on their side, not yours.

Better Proposals found 37.7% of proposals were first opened on a phone (2020). You designed for A4. They first meet it on a six-inch screen. A Recto link opens as plain slides, a page-turning book or a magazine spread, so you choose how that first look happens.

Big invoices wait longest. Bonsai found invoices over $20,000 were three times more likely to be paid late than invoices under $100. On a big project, don't send one big invoice. Split it: a deposit up front, milestones along the way.

Arabic script has no capital letters. In English, capitals do much of the hierarchy: headings, names, emphasis. In Kurdish and Arabic that job falls to size, weight and space. If your English headings lean on ALL CAPS, the other side of the page needs its own plan.

Agencies in the ANA and 4A's study put an average of 11 people on a new-business pitch, and 18 when defending an existing account (2023). Before you say yes to the next one, count the people, not just the hours.

People read about 20% of the words on a web page. Jakob Nielsen's 2008 analysis put the ceiling at 28%. Assume your proposal gets the same treatment on screen. Headings, short paragraphs and one bold number do more than a perfect paragraph nobody reaches.

About a third of agencies decline pitches where they aren't the incumbent, according to ANA and 4A's research (2023). Saying no to a pitch is normal. The question is which ones: budget, fit, and whether they'll pay for the thinking.

Revisions are buying signals. Proposify found one round of revisions came with an 18% higher close rate, two rounds with 28% (2026). Make rounds easy. In Recto, clients pin a comment to the exact spot on the page, no account needed. Nobody has to describe where the problem is.

In Bonsai's invoice data, 31% of invoices from women freelancers were paid late, against 24% for men and 23% for studios, even after controlling for skills, experience and client size. Worth knowing. Worth saying out loud.

Open Page: Better Proposals found sending on Monday gave only a 1.1% edge, and Friday sends took about a day longer to sign. So the day barely matters. What does? Tell us one thing you changed that actually moved your win rate.

Ask for the deposit with the yes. In Better Proposals' 2020 data, 67% of proposals that asked for payment through an integration got it, and the average time from signature to payment was 7 hours 43 minutes.

In 2012 Errol Morris tested about 45,000 New York Times readers: the same passage, six fonts. Baskerville drew the most agreement and the least disagreement. Not a lab study, and Morris said so. But type has a voice before the words do.

A pitch costs the client too. ANA and the 4A's estimate a client spends about $400,000 running an agency pitch, and about $1 million in total when three agencies are finalists (2023). Clients don't run reviews lightly. Treat the brief like the investment it is.

Buyers come back. Proposify found winning proposals were viewed 12 times on average, losing ones 8 (2026). In Recto you see who viewed your link, the time on each page and how far they got. When someone returns to the pricing page twice, that's your follow-up.

Bonsai's late-payment rates by work type: developers 29%, designers 28%, writers 26%, photographers 24%. Whatever you do, roughly one invoice in four arrives late. Put the due date and the deposit on page one of the proposal, not in the small print.

Numbers run left to right, even inside right-to-left text. ٢٥٠ and 250 are both read from the left, in the middle of a Kurdish or Arabic sentence that reads from the right. Prices, dates and phone numbers are where bilingual layouts usually break. Check them first.

54% of agency respondents told ANA and the 4A's that being put up for review had a major or moderate impact on their decision to resign the account (2023). A review tests the relationship before it tests the work.

Only 20% of proposals include video, Proposify found. When the buyer watches it, the proposal is 3.3x more likely to close (2026). Short, personal, near the top. Thirty seconds of you explaining the idea beats three pages describing it.

Price the after. Proposify saw an 18x lift in deal value on proposals with recurring fees (2026). Better Proposals found monthly fees sold for 28.5% more than one-off fees (2020). If the work continues after launch, the proposal should say so.

Bonsai found 90% of late invoices were paid within a month of the due date. Most late payers aren't refusing. They forgot. A Recto invoice moves from draft to sent, viewed, overdue and paid, so you know who opened it and who needs a nudge.

Half of freelancers had trouble collecting payment in a single year. Freelancers Union found 50% struggled in 2014. Of those, 81% were paid late and 34% weren't paid at all for at least one job. A contract isn't paranoia. It's manners, in writing.

Open Page: when clients pay agencies to pitch, it's most often reimbursed expenses (70%), a flat fee (57%) or payment for spec work (46%), per ANA and 4A's research. Studios and freelancers: have you ever been paid to pitch? How did you ask?

Agency reviews average about 2.5 months when the incumbent takes part and 3.2 months when it doesn't, according to clients in the ANA and 4A's study. Waiting on a yes? Silence isn't a no. It's usually a calendar.

Give the client something to fill in. Proposify's 2026 data puts the close rate of proposals with client input forms at 41%, against a 34% average. A start date, a package choice, a name for the project. Filling in turns reading into deciding.

Proposals with discounts had a 75% higher average value in Proposify's data: $20K up to $35K (2026). Bigger deals attract discounts, so don't read it as cause. Read it as craft: show the full price first, then the reduction.

The first number sets the frame. In Tversky and Kahneman's 1974 experiment, people who watched a wheel stop on 65 guessed far more African countries were in the UN than people who saw 10. In a Recto pricing table, lead with the full scope. Everything after reads against it.

32% of UK freelancers had a client pay late in the past year, according to IPSE's Freelancer Confidence Index (Q1 2024). In 2022 it was 35%. Barely moving. The fix is still in the paperwork: due dates, deposits, written terms.

Right-to-left isn't just left-to-right mirrored. Reading starts top right, so the logo, page numbers and the 'next' arrow move. But URLs, emails and English names inside the line still run left to right. Good bilingual design handles both directions in one sentence.

In 1927 Bluma Zeigarnik found people remember unfinished tasks better than finished ones. Ending a deck on 'Thank you' closes the loop. Ending on the open question, the decision you need from them, leaves something to think about on the drive home.

Typographers recommend 45 to 75 characters per line for body text. Robert Bringhurst calls 66 the ideal. Longer, and the eye gets lost on the way back to the next line. A4 set edge to edge at 10pt can run past 100. Widen the margins, not the text.

In Iyengar and Lepper's jam study (2000), a table of 24 jams drew more shoppers, but only 3% bought. With 6 jams, 30% did. Choice attracts. Too much choice stalls. Three packages in a proposal, not seven.

Buyers open 80% of the proposals they go on to reject, Proposify found (2026). An open isn't interest. Time and return visits are. Recto shows the time on each page and how far they got. Someone who stopped at the price page is telling you something.

Defending costs double. ANA and the 4A's put the average cost of a pitch at $406,092 for the incumbent agency, against $204,461 for an outsider (2023). Keep the relationship warm enough that you never have to defend it.

Open Page: Upwork counted 64 million Americans doing freelance work in 2023, 38% of the US workforce. Freelancers and studios in Kurdistan and Iraq: how did you land your first client? The path here is different, and someone starting out needs to hear yours.

Daniel Kahneman's peak-end rule: we judge an experience mostly by its most intense moment and by how it ends. A proposal ends on terms, a payment schedule and a signature. Make the last page as considered as the cover.

Nielsen Norman Group's eye-tracking found people scan pages in an F shape: across the top, across again, then down the left edge. So the first words of each line matter most. 'Deposit: 40%' gets read. 'We would kindly ask for a deposit of 40%' gets skipped.

Dan Ariely's decoy test: web-only $59, print-only $125, print and web $125. 84% chose print and web. Remove the print-only option, which nobody chose, and only 32% did. The option nobody picks still shapes the choice. Design your middle package with care.

Proposify's average proposal takes 17 minutes to create (2026). Speed only helps if it still looks like you. Recto templates start from your brand kit: logos, colours and fonts applied to the whole document in one click.

In the UK, the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 lets small businesses charge 8% above the Bank of England base rate on late business-to-business invoices. Wherever you work, put your late-payment terms in writing before the work starts.

One language, two scripts. In Iraq and Iran, Kurdish is mostly written in an Arabic-based script. In Turkey and Syria, Kurmanji is written in the Latin Hawar alphabet, with letters like ç, ê, î, ş and û. A Kurdish brand with readers on both sides may need both.

The average deal won through Proposify was worth $16,388 (2026). Most proposals take under twenty minutes to make. That's a five-figure document, built in less time than a lunch break. Spend the extra hour.

A4 is 210 by 297 mm, and every ISO paper size keeps the same 1:√2 ratio. Fold A4 in half and you get A5 with identical proportions. A proposal designed on A4 scales down to an A5 leave-behind without a single layout change.

Half of clients who run agency reviews say the main short-term benefit is that 'a new agency is highly motivated to deliver' (ANA and 4A's, 2023). Motivation is part of what they're buying. Show it: put a plan for the first 30 days in the proposal.

Proposify found proposals that went through three rounds of revisions closed 45% more often (2026). Revisions are normal. Version chaos isn't. A Recto link updates when you edit, so the client always opens the latest version and nobody asks for v4_FINAL.
One in four incumbent agencies declined to take part in a pitch to keep their client's business, according to ANA and 4A's research (2023). Walking away from a review is a decision, not a defeat.

Open Page: 62% of clients in ANA and 4A's research named price as the top factor when choosing an agency. So: price on page one, or make them read the thinking first? Make your case. We'll read every one.

Presenters: the '7% words, 38% voice, 55% body language' rule comes from Albert Mehrabian's 1967 experiments on single words carrying feelings. Mehrabian has said it doesn't apply to ordinary communication. Your words matter. Put them on the page, not just in the room.

George Miller's 1956 'magical number seven' is quoted everywhere. Later research by Nelson Cowan (2001) puts working memory closer to four chunks. Four packages, four steps, four numbers on a slide. Past that, people stop holding and start skimming.

Order matters in a pitch line-up. Wändi Bruine de Bruin's 2005 study of Eurovision and figure skating found later performers got higher scores. If the client lets you choose a slot, ask to go last. If you can't, end on your strongest page.

Your proposal will be forwarded, and you can't control where it goes. A Recto link can carry a password and an expiry date, and you can unpublish it any time. If the deal goes quiet, the pricing doesn't stay out in the world.

IPSE's research found freelancers hold back from chasing invoices or charging interest because they fear looking 'difficult' and losing the relationship. A clear payment schedule in the proposal does the chasing for you. The terms were agreed before anyone was late.

Arabic-script text set at the same point size as Latin often looks smaller, because the letters sit differently around the baseline. On a bilingual page, size the Kurdish or Arabic by eye until both lines look equally important, not by matching numbers.

In 2003 Edward Tufte showed how a Boeing slide for NASA about the Columbia foam strike buried the key warning under nested bullet points. Bullets hide relationships between ideas. If something matters, give it a sentence, not a bullet.

Richard Mayer's research on multimedia learning found people learn less when the same words are on screen and spoken at the same time. It's called the redundancy effect. Presenters: if you'll say it, don't also put the paragraph on the slide.

In Anderson and Simester's 2003 field test, a dress priced at $39 outsold the same dress at $34. Price endings carry meaning. In client work, round numbers read as considered, precise ones as calculated. Choose on purpose.

45% of clients in ANA and 4A's research named creative execution as a top factor in choosing an agency, second only to price. Show the work the way it ran. Recto case study blocks hold the before and after, the metrics and a testimonial on one page.
C. Northcote Parkinson, 1955: work expands to fill the time available for its completion. That's true for feedback too. Give every revision round a date, not just a number.
Open Page: Proposify's 2026 data says proposals with three revision rounds closed 45% more often than those with none. How many rounds do you include before you start charging? And how do you say it?

Precise anchors stick. Janiszewski and Uy (2008) found people adjusted less from a precise number like $4,988 than from a round $5,000. On a rate card, a number that looks calculated looks less negotiable.

The picture superiority effect: people remember pictures better than words, a finding Allan Paivio explained in the 1970s with his dual-coding theory. The page they remember from your proposal will probably be an image. Choose which one.

The serial position effect: people remember the first and last items in a list best. In a proposal with three case studies, put the strongest first and the second strongest last. The middle one is the safest place for the weakest.

New in Recto Studio: folio. You finish an identity, then spend another day making the presentation. Upload the logo, guidelines and mockups, and one click turns them into an animated presentation page in that brand, built on your device and downloaded as one file.
Freelancers in the US earned $1.27 trillion in 2023, according to Upwork's Freelance Forward report. That isn't a side economy. Charge like you're part of it.

Arabic-script letters change shape depending on where they sit: isolated, initial, medial or final. That's why you can't letter-space Kurdish or Arabic like English. Tracking breaks the joins. Let the words breathe with space between them, not inside them.
The last slide of most decks says 'Thank you' and an email address. The recency effect says the last thing they see is what they'll remember. End on the decision you want them to make.
